'''Emanuel Miller''' (born June 19, 2000) is a Canadian professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Austin Spurs]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M Aggies]] and the [[TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball|TCU Horned Frogs]].

==Early life==
Miller began his high school career at [[Bill Crothers Secondary School]]. Prior to his junior season, he transferred to [[La Lumiere School]].<ref>{{cite news |date=July 24, 2017 |title=La Lumiere (Ind.) adds top five 2019 Canadian prospect Emanuel Miller |url=https://www.usatodayhss.com/story/sports/high-school/2017/07/24/la-lumiere-ind-adds-top-five-2019-canadian-prospect-emanuel-miller/76903873007/ |access-date=August 4, 2021 |work=[[USA Today]]}}</ref> Miller transferred to [[Prolific Prep]] for his senior season. In October 2018, he committed to [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech]] over offers from [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]], [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]], and [[Buffalo Bulls men's basketball|Buffalo]].<ref name=evans>{{cite web|first=Corey|last=Evans|title=Rivals150 forward Emanuel Miller commits to Virginia Tech|url=https://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/news/rivals150-forward-emanuel-miller-commits-to-virginia-tech|website=Rivals.com|date=October 18, 2018|access-date=August 4, 2021}}</ref> After [[Buzz Williams]] accepted the head coaching position at [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M]], Miller followed him to play for the Aggies.<ref>{{cite news|first=Hannah|last=Underwood|title=5 things to know about Texas A&M F Emanuel Miller, including his leadership on and off the court|url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/texas-am-aggies/2021/01/11/5-things-to-know-about-texas-am-f-emanuel-miller-miller-leads-aggies-on-off-court-in-sophomore-season/|work=[[The Dallas Morning News]]|date=January 11, 2021|access-date=August 4, 2021}}</ref>

==College career==
Miller averaged 6.4 points and 6.3 rebounds per game as a freshman.<ref>{{cite news|title=K-State to Host Texas A&M in SEC/Big 12 Challenge|url=https://www.ksal.com/k-state-to-host-texas-am-in-sec-big-12-challenge/|work=KSAL|date=October 21, 2020|access-date=August 4, 2021}}</ref> On January 26, 2021, he scored a career-high 28 points in a 78–54 loss to [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Lawson scores 30, leads South Carolina over Texas A&M 78-54|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401258733|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=January 6, 2021|access-date=August 4, 2021}}</ref> As a sophomore, Miller averaged 16.2 points and 8.2 rebounds per game. Following the season, he transferred to [[TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball|TCU]], citing the desire of a fresh start.<ref>{{cite news|first=Travis|last=Brown|title=Former Texas A&M forward Emanuel Miller transferring to TCU|url=https://theeagle.com/sports/college/aggiesports/mens_basketball/former-texas-a-m-forward-emanuel-miller-transferring-to-tcu/article_810ae68e-a968-11eb-a2c2-db89fa277389.html|work=[[The Bryan-College Station Eagle]]|date=April 29, 2021|access-date=August 4, 2021}}</ref> Miller averaged 10.3 points and 6.2 rebounds per game in his junior season.<ref>{{cite news|title=No. 14 TCU has stable roster and highest preseason ranking|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2022/10/21/no-14-tcu-has-stable-roster-and-highest-preseason-ranking/50860221/|work=[[USA Today]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=October 21, 2022|access-date=July 14, 2024}}</ref> As a senior, he averaged 12.3 points and 6.5 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite news|first=Steven|last=Johnson|title=Dallas Mavericks bringing in former TCU star Emanuel Miller for pre-NBA Draft workout|url=https://www.star-telegram.com/sports/article289410996.html|work=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]]|date=June 20, 2024|access-date=July 14, 2024}}</ref> In his final season, Miller averaged 15.8 points and 6.1 rebounds per game. He was named to the Second Team All-[[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Nicholas|last=Girimonte|title=Likely NBA Draft Landing Spots for Emanuel Miller|url=https://www.si.com/college/tcu/basketball/likely-nba-draft-landing-spots-for-emanuel-miller-01j1129hzce7|work=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=June 23, 2024|access-date=July 14, 2024}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Texas Legends (2024)===
After going undrafted in the [[2024 NBA draft]], Miller signed with the [[Dallas Mavericks]] on July 12, 2024, and joined them for the [[2024 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite tweet|first=Mike|last=Curtis|title=Mavs announce they’ve signed guard Jazian Gortman and forward Emanuel Miller. Both players will play for the team’s Summer League squad. Mavs SL coach Jared Dudley said today that Miller is one of the most physical players on the team.|number=1811913501071540495|user=MikeACurtis2|date=July 12, 2024|access-date=July 13, 2024}}</ref> However, he was waived by the Mavericks on October 18<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Mavs PR|title=The Dallas Mavericks announced today they have waived guard AJ Lawson, forward Emanuel Miller and center Jamarion Sharp.|number=1847306706323132821|user=MavsPR|date=October 18, 2024|access-date=October 20, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Doyle|last=Rader|title=Dallas Mavericks Waive AJ Lawson, Emanuel Miller And Jamarion Sharp|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/doylerader/2024/10/18/dallas-mavericks-waive-aj-lawson-emanuel-miller-and-jamarion-sharp/|website=Forbes.com|date=October 18, 2024|access-date=October 19, 2024}}</ref> and on October 26, he joined the [[Texas Legends]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Texas Legends Finalize 2024-25 Training Camp Roster Following NBA G League Draft|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/texas-legends-finalize-2024-25-training-camp-roster-following-nba-g-league-draft/n-6159950|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 26, 2024|access-date=October 26, 2024}}</ref>

===Chicago Bulls (2024–2026)===
On December 28, 2024, Miller signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Bulls sign Emanuel Miller to two-way contract|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-emanuel-miller-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=December 28, 2024|access-date=December 28, 2024}}</ref> He made six appearances for the Bulls during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 1.7 points, 1.3 rebounds, and 0.3 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Emanuel Miller 2024-25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4432872/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=June 23, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

Miller played in five contests for the Bulls during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], recording averages of 3.0 points, 0.6 rebounds, and 0.8 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Emanuel Miller 2025-26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4432872/type/nba/year/2026|access-date=June 23, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

===Austin Spurs (2026)===
On February 1, 2026, Miller was traded to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in a three-team trade that also included the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-02-01 |title=Cleveland Completes Three-Team Trade with Sacramento and Chicago |url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/releases-dennis-schroder-keon-ellis-260201 |access-date=2026-02-03 |website=NBA.com |language=en-US}}</ref> He was released by the Cavaliers on February 20, without making an appearance for the team.<ref>{{cite web|title= Cavaliers Sign Darius Brown to Two-Way Contract |url= https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/releases-darius-brown-260220 |website=NBA.com|date=February 20, 2026|access-date=April 11, 2026}}</ref> On February 23, the [[San Antonio Spurs]] signed Miller to a two-way contract.<ref>{{Cite web|title=The San Antonio Spurs Sign Emanuel Miller To A Two-Way Contract|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/the-san-antonio-spurs-sign-emanuel-miller-to-a-two-way-contract|access-date=April 10, 2026|website=gleague.nba.com|language=en}}</ref> He did not make any appearances for San Antonio prior to being waived on July 22.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Spurs move on from young player to continue investing in David Jones-Garcia|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/spurs-move-one-young-player-170951975.html|access-date=August 25, 2026|website=sports.yahoo.com|language=en}}</ref>

==National team career==
Miller has represented [[Canada men's national under-19 basketball team|Canada]] in several international competitions. In July 2017, he competed for the Canada team that won a gold medal at the [[2017 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|FIBA U19 World Cup]]. Miller averaged 1.6 points and 1.7 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite news|first=Travis|last=Brown|title=Canadian Emanuel Miller beginning to shine for Aggie men|url=https://theeagle.com/sports/canadian-emanuel-miller-beginning-to-shine-for-aggie-men/article_c67b122a-52de-11ea-b0af-47d879e510de.html|work=[[The Bryan-College Station Eagle]]|date=February 19, 2020|access-date=August 4, 2021}}</ref> In June 2018, he was a key piece for the Canada team that captured a silver medal at the [[2018 FIBA Under-18 Americas Championship|FIBA U18 Americas Championship]]. Miller averaged 17.3 points, 7.3 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 1.2 steals per game.<ref name=evans/> In the semifinal win against Puerto Rico, he posted 31 points and 14 rebounds.<ref>{{cite news|title=In the region: Basketball recruit Emanuel Miller picks Virginia Tech|url=https://roanoke.com/sports/college/va_tech/in-the-region-basketball-recruit-emanuel-miller-picks-virginia-tech/article_7fbfdaa1-2854-5fb8-94dc-dd1c64dea355.html|work=[[The Roanoke Times]]|date=October 18, 2018|access-date=August 4, 2021}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Miller's younger brother [[Leonard Miller (basketball)|Leonard]]<ref name=backus>{{cite web|first=Will|last=Backus|title=Leonard Miller, uncommitted prospect in 2022 class, declares for NBA Draft|url=https://247sports.com/Article/Leonard-Miller-uncommitted-prospect-in-2022-class-declares-for-NBA-Draft-186654105/|work=[[247Sports]]|date=April 23, 2022|access-date=June 11, 2022}}</ref> plays for the [[Chicago Bulls]] of the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]], after being traded by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]],  whom he was drafted by in the second round of the [[2023 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Timberwolves Sign Leonard Miller|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-sign-leonard-miller|website=NBA.com|date=July 9, 2023|access-date=July 9, 2023}}</ref>
